newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Constraints seen on more Australia Internet usage.
newsitem.headline: Constraints seen on more Australia Internet usage.

text.p: The number of Australians using the Internet has grown strongly in recent years but high access costs, long delays and family commitments are seen as the main barriers to greater Internet use, a new survey said on Monday.
The third www.consult survey of Australian Internet users found that Australia's 1.35 million Internet users mainly used the Internet for entertainment, e-mail and research.

"Response times, family life, time constraints, and access costs remain the key hurdles to greater Internet use," Ramin Marzbani, www.consult principal and Internet industry analyst, said in a statement.
"There is a slow increase in the proportion of female Internet users, who make up less than 20 percent of users," Marzbani said.
The www.consult survey said that although significant proportions of Internet users had tried online shopping, this was still not a driver of Internet use.
But, it said attitudes towards electronic transactions were very positive with less than 15 percent indicating a reluctance to try online transactions.

The survey said 48 percent of Internet users claim they would book and pay for travel online and a significant number indicated willingness to book online using payment systems other than credit cards.
A www.consult spokeswoman said that of the 1.35 million Internet users in Australia, 790,000 were commercial users, split between business and home users, with the remainder in the academic field.
The survey said Australia had Internet service providers (ISPs), as of the first quarter of 1997, up from 16 in 1993.
The survey, involving more than 8,600 repondents, was conducted between April and June.
